subject.title: fix: stabilize embedded prompt caching across policy and Responses boundaries

question: Should non-owner and ambient turns keep protected core-tool schemas model-visible when immutable current-turn policy denies their execution before hooks and side effects?
rationale: The implementation is coherent and well-proven, but tool visibility versus execution authority is an intentional security boundary that tests and automated review cannot authorize for maintainers.

options.title: Approve stable visible schemas
options.body: Keep the schemas stable for prompt-cache reuse and require immutable policy plus pre-execution denial on every runtime path.

options.title: Retain hidden schemas
options.body: Preserve sender-specific schema filtering and accept reduced cache reuse so denied capabilities remain absent from model context.

recommendation.title: Approve stable visible schemas
recommendation.body: Keep the schemas stable for prompt-cache reuse and require immutable policy plus pre-execution denial on every runtime path.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest combined history across native Responses selection, Codex supervision, and the affected embedded runtime.
